title: Add local-only shopping cart prototype to On The Hook mobile app
description:
Implement a fully local shopping-cart and prototype order-submission flow in the existing shared React Native On The Hook iOS/Android app. Customers can add bundled Menu items to a cart, change quantities, review the cart, tap Submit Order, see a local confirmation screen, and then have the cart cleared.

This epic intentionally changes the earlier prototype scope that treated ordering as external-only / prohibited native cart behavior. For this epic, a native cart is explicitly allowed and required, but ONLY as an on-device prototype. No order is transmitted anywhere.

Hard architecture constraint: the entire feature must function with networking disabled. Do not add or call an OTH backend, ordering-provider API, payment API, tax API, authentication API, analytics endpoint, website scraper, WebView ordering flow, or any other HTTP/network service. Existing OS-native integrations elsewhere in the app are unrelated and must not be pulled into the cart flow.

Bundled prototype pricing is supplied in `oth-menu-pricing.json`. Treat that file as the authoritative cart pricing fixture for this prototype. Do not block implementation waiting for remote menu/bootstrap/pricing services.
acceptance_criteria:
- All child beads are complete and closed.
- A user can add valid bundled Menu items to the cart, including multiple quantities.
- The cart survives normal app navigation and app restart through local persistence.
- Cart totals are calculated deterministically from integer cents; floating-point money arithmetic is not used.
- A user can edit quantities, remove individual lines, and clear the cart.
- Submit Order creates an in-memory/local confirmation receipt snapshot, clears the cart, and navigates to a confirmation screen.
- Confirmation clearly states that this prototype did not transmit a real restaurant order.
- Returning to Menu after confirmation shows an empty cart and zero badge count.
- No cart/order code performs HTTP calls or requires any backend/API configuration.
- iOS and Android share the same domain/store/UI implementation except for normal platform-specific presentation details.
- Existing Find Us schedule order-link behavior is not repurposed or scraped; this epic is a Menu-cart prototype only.
- `oth-menu-pricing.json` is accepted as authoritative prototype pricing; implementation does not wait for a remote pricing source.
notes: This requirement supersedes stale repository wording that says native cart/checkout is forbidden. It does NOT authorize payments or real order transmission. Keep the feature isolated enough that a future real OrderSubmissionService can replace the local submitter without rewriting Menu or Cart UI.

title: Normalize purchasable bundled Menu data and remove stale cart prohibitions
description:
Use the supplied bundled `oth-menu-pricing.json` as the authoritative pricing source for the standalone cart prototype. Integrate its stable IDs and integer `priceCents` values with the existing bundled Menu content. Do not scrape the website at runtime and do not wait for a backend, bootstrap service, first-party API, or location-specific price service.

If the existing Menu already contains matching names/descriptions/assets, preserve those presentation fields and merge the fixture's IDs/prices. Variant entries in the fixture (cod piece count and chowder size) may be represented as separate purchasable rows/options using the simplest approach consistent with the current Menu UI. Add-ons listed in the fixture are reference data only and are explicitly out of scope for this cart prototype.

The fixture intentionally uses prototype baseline prices because public OTH ordering prices can vary by location. That variation is NOT a blocker for this standalone prototype.
acceptance_criteria:
- `oth-menu-pricing.json` is loaded/bundled locally and requires no runtime network access.
- Every prototype cart-eligible item uses the fixture's stable non-empty id and integer priceCents.
- Existing Menu names/descriptions/images are preserved where they already exist.
- Variant products use the explicit fixture prices; no runtime currency-string parsing is used.
- Location-specific public price variation is documented but does not block prototype implementation.
- The implementation MUST NOT wait for or call an API/bootstrap/order-provider service to obtain prices.
- The implementation MUST NOT scrape the public website at runtime.
- Add-ons/modifiers in the fixture remain out of scope for the prototype cart unless separately requested.
- Existing event Order Now / external URL handling remains independent from Menu cart behavior.
notes: This bead is no longer allowed to block on absent first-party pricing/menu APIs. `oth-menu-pricing.json` is sufficient production-like fixture data for acceptance.

title: Implement deterministic cart domain model, reducer, selectors, and money calculations
description:
Implement the platform-neutral cart domain/state logic. Reuse the repository's existing state-management approach if one already exists. If it does not, use a small React Context + useReducer/store abstraction rather than introducing a heavy global state framework solely for this feature.

Recommended logical state:
- hydrated: boolean so UI does not overwrite persisted data before hydration completes.
- quantities keyed by stable menuItemId, or equivalent normalized lines.
- optional submit-in-progress guard.

Persist only durable cart intent (menuItemId + quantity), then resolve current name/price from the authoritative bundled Menu data. Computed CartLine view data should expose menuItemId, name, unitPriceCents, quantity, and lineTotalCents. This prevents stale persisted price/name snapshots after a future app/menu update.

Required actions: add one, increment, decrement, set quantity, remove line, clear cart, hydrate/replace from persisted data. Quantity must always be a positive integer for stored lines. Removing/decrementing to zero removes the line. Use a reasonable hard defensive maximum of 99 units per item and prevent overflow rather than wrapping.

Required selectors: distinct line count, total unit count for badges, subtotalCents, empty state, resolved lines in deterministic menu/cart order. Use integer arithmetic only.
acceptance_criteria:
- Adding the same menuItemId increments one line instead of creating duplicate lines.
- Quantity is always an integer from 1 through 99 for an existing line.
- Decrementing quantity 1 removes the line cleanly.
- remove and clear operations are idempotent.
- totalUnitCount is the sum of quantities and is used for the cart badge.
- subtotalCents equals the exact sum of unitPriceCents * quantity for all resolved lines.
- No JavaScript floating-point dollar calculations are used.
- Persisted identifiers that no longer exist in bundled Menu data are ignored/removed during reconciliation.
- Current bundled price/name wins when resolving a persisted cart after an app/menu update.
- Domain logic contains no React Navigation, HTTP, payment, tax, or ordering-provider concerns.
- Unit tests cover add/increment/decrement/set/remove/clear, max quantity, stale item reconciliation, badge count, and subtotal.
notes: Do not use menu display strings as keys. Keep money in cents end-to-end until the presentation formatter.

title: Persist and hydrate cart locally with a versioned storage schema
description:
Add local cart persistence so items survive normal app restarts. Use the repository's existing local persistence abstraction. If none exists, use @react-native-async-storage/async-storage or the already-installed equivalent; adding a local storage package is allowed, adding a service/backend is not.

Use one versioned key such as 'oth.cart.v1'. Suggested payload:
{ schemaVersion: 1, items: [{ menuItemId: string, quantity: integer }], updatedAt: ISO timestamp }

Do not persist calculated subtotal, item display price, full Menu objects, confirmation receipts, customer identity, location, payment data, or anything sensitive. On hydration, validate shape and ranges, reconcile IDs against current bundled Menu data, drop invalid/unknown lines, and continue with a usable empty/partial cart rather than crashing.

Writes should occur after cart mutations through one repository/service boundary. Avoid a race where initial empty state is persisted before hydration completes. Clearing the cart must remove/replace the persisted payload immediately enough that a successful local Submit Order cannot resurrect old lines after app restart.
acceptance_criteria:
- Cart contents and quantities survive app restart locally.
- Storage payload has explicit schemaVersion 1 and contains only menuItemId, quantity, and harmless metadata.
- Initial empty state is not written over persisted cart data before hydration finishes.
- Malformed JSON/storage data does not crash the app; it is discarded or safely repaired.
- Unknown removed menuItemIds are dropped during hydration/reconciliation.
- Invalid quantities (0, negative, non-integer, >99) are rejected/clamped according to one documented deterministic policy.
- clearCart removes persisted cart intent so the next cold launch is empty.
- Storage failures produce a recoverable local error/log path and do not trigger networking.
- Persistence tests cover cold hydration, mutation persistence, corrupted payload, schema mismatch, stale menu item, and clear.
notes: A future storage migration can introduce oth.cart.v2. For now, unsupported future schema versions should fail safe rather than guessing.

title: Add polished Add to Cart and quantity controls to the Menu
description:
Integrate cart actions into the existing branded Menu without redesigning the entire screen. Every purchasable Menu item should make its price and cart action obvious. Preserve existing category structure (for example Entrees, Sides, Drinks) and existing On The Hook visual tokens.

Default interaction:
- Item not in cart: clear 'Add to Cart' or compact '+ Add' action.
- Item in cart: show current quantity and allow another add; a compact minus / quantity / plus stepper is preferred where it fits without making rows noisy.
- Non-purchasable/missing-price item: no functional add action; present existing menu information honestly.
- Give immediate visual/state feedback after add without modal spam.

Do not require a store/truck selection to add items for this prototype. Do not attach the cart to a Find Us event. Do not add customizations/modifiers, special instructions, taxes, tips, coupons, or payment fields in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each valid priced Menu item can be added with one explicit tap.
- Repeated add actions update the existing line quantity.
- Current quantity is visible for items already in the cart without navigating away.
- Quantity controls honor the 1..99 domain rules and accessible disabled states.
- Price formatting matches US dollars and uses shared money formatting from integer cents.
- Menu scroll position/category navigation remains stable while adding items.
- Controls meet practical 44x44 minimum touch targets and expose meaningful accessibility labels/roles/values.
- Adding items requires no network, location, account, or event selection.
- Component tests cover first add, repeated add, decrement/removal if shown inline, max quantity, and non-purchasable item state.
notes: Prefer the existing Button/IconButton/typography/card primitives. Do not create a second visual design system for cart UI.

title: Build Cart screen with editing, subtotal, empty state, and clear action
description:
Create a dedicated Cart screen using the existing navigation and design system. It must be useful as both a review screen and an editing screen.

Each cart line shows item name, formatted unit price, quantity control, line total, and remove action. The summary shows total unit count and Subtotal. Do NOT invent sales tax, fees, discounts, tips, or a final tax-inclusive Total because no tax/location service exists. The primary CTA is 'Submit Order' as requested, but this remains a prototype local action.

Empty state: branded concise message plus a 'Browse Menu' action. Provide a secondary 'Clear Cart' action when non-empty; use a confirmation alert/dialog before destructive full clear unless the app's established UX has an equivalent undo pattern.

The screen must handle hydration state without flashing a false empty cart. It must remain usable with long item names, large Dynamic Type, and a cart large enough to scroll.
acceptance_criteria:
- Cart screen lists every resolved line exactly once with unit price, quantity, and line total.
- Plus/minus and remove update Menu-visible quantities and badge state immediately through the same shared store.
- Summary Subtotal is derived from the cart selector and formats exactly to two USD decimal places.
- No tax, service fee, tip, discount, or payment estimate is fabricated.
- Submit Order is disabled when cart is empty, not hydrated, or currently submitting.
- Empty cart has a clear Browse Menu CTA.
- Clear Cart requires deliberate confirmation/undo-equivalent and leaves a persisted empty cart.
- Large carts scroll while primary actions remain reachable using safe-area-aware layout.
- Screen is accessible with VoiceOver/TalkBack labels for item quantity, increment, decrement, remove, subtotal, clear, and submit.
- Component tests cover empty, one-line, multi-line, quantity edits, removal, clear confirmation, disabled submit, and long content.
notes: Keep the summary honest: this prototype knows item subtotal only.

title: Integrate Cart navigation, badge, and back behavior into the app shell
description:
Make Cart discoverable without destabilizing the current Home / Find Us / Menu / More primary navigation. Prefer a cart icon with badge in the top-level/app header and at minimum on Menu. If the existing shell makes a consistent global header action straightforward, expose it on all top-level screens; do not add a fifth bottom tab solely for this prototype unless the current navigation conventions clearly require it.

The badge displays total units, not distinct line count. Hide the badge entirely when zero. For counts above the practical badge width, display '99+' while retaining the actual domain count internally.

Add typed routes/screens for Cart and OrderConfirmation. Back from Cart should return to the prior screen normally. Confirmation navigation semantics are handled by the submit bead so a completed order does not navigate back into the pre-submit cart state.
acceptance_criteria:
- Cart is reachable from Menu in one tap without burying it under More.
- Where a shared top-level header exists, Cart access is consistently available without duplicating state logic per screen.
- Badge equals total quantity across all cart lines, hides at zero, and visually caps at 99+.
- Badge updates immediately on add/remove/quantity change and after hydration.
- Cart icon/button has an accessibility label including current item count when nonzero.
- Cart and OrderConfirmation are typed/named routes consistent with existing navigation architecture.
- Existing Home, Find Us, Menu, More, Event Detail, and deep/back navigation continue to work.
- No navigation action performs a network call.
notes: Do not confuse this cart badge with notification badges or event Order Now state.

title: Implement local Submit Order transaction and confirmation screen
description:
Implement the prototype submission flow with a clean future integration seam but no real transport. Introduce an OrderSubmissionService/OrderSubmitter interface (or equivalent existing service abstraction) used by the UI. Its only current implementation is LocalOrderSubmissionService and MUST NOT call fetch, axios, WebView, payment SDKs, URL linking, or any backend.

On Submit Order:
1. Reject empty/unhydrated submission.
2. Disable the button immediately to prevent double-submit.
3. Snapshot immutable receipt data from current resolved lines: item name, unitPriceCents, quantity, lineTotalCents, subtotalCents, and submittedAt. This receipt is local UI state only and is not order history.
4. Clear in-memory cart and persisted cart intent exactly once.
5. Navigate with replace/reset semantics to OrderConfirmation carrying the immutable receipt snapshot so the confirmation remains visible even though the live cart is now empty.

Confirmation UI should use On The Hook branding, show a concise summary/subtotal, and contain explicit prototype language such as 'Prototype order confirmed' and 'No order was transmitted to a restaurant.' Do not display a fake restaurant order number, pickup time, payment status, or fulfillment promise. Provide 'Back to Menu' as the main exit action.
acceptance_criteria:
- Submit Order never invokes HTTP, external URL, WebView, payment SDK, location service, authentication, or event-order provider code.
- Double tapping Submit Order produces one local receipt/transition and one cart clear.
- Receipt is snapshotted before clearing and confirmation still shows all submitted lines and subtotal afterward.
- Live cart state and persisted cart are empty before/when confirmation is presented.
- Relaunching the app after successful local submission does not restore the submitted cart.
- Confirmation plainly states that no real restaurant order was transmitted.
- Confirmation does not invent tax, final charged total, order number, pickup location/time, payment state, or fulfillment status.
- Back navigation cannot resurrect the populated pre-submit Cart screen; Back to Menu leads to Menu with zero badge.
- Local submission service is replaceable later through one interface/boundary rather than being embedded in screen code.
- Tests cover successful submit, double-submit guard, empty submit prevention, persistence clear, receipt immutability, and navigation reset.
notes: The interface is for future replacement, not justification to create a speculative backend client now.

title: Harden cart UX, accessibility, persistence edge cases, and error recovery
description:
Perform a focused quality pass across Menu cart controls, badge, Cart, persistence, and OrderConfirmation. Fix edge cases rather than papering them over with disabled features.

Required cases include: corrupted storage; removed menu item after app update; changed menu price after app update; storage write failure; rapid add taps; rapid plus/minus taps; max quantity; app background/foreground; screen rotation where relevant; Dynamic Type; long menu item names; screen readers; reduce motion; and safe-area/keyboard behavior (although checkout has no text fields).

If local persistence fails, the app may keep the in-memory cart usable for the current session but must present/log a clear recoverable state according to existing app error conventions. Do not silently introduce cloud sync as a fix.
acceptance_criteria:
- Rapid interactions cannot create duplicate lines, negative quantities, or values above 99.
- Corrupted/stale persisted data cannot crash Menu or Cart.
- Current bundled Menu data resolves price/name after hydration, so changed prices are reflected before submission.
- Missing menu items are removed from cart instead of displaying ghost lines.
- Persistence failure does not trigger network fallback and does not make the entire app unusable.
- All cart controls expose correct accessibility role, label, state/value, and practical tap target sizing.
- Dynamic Type / large text keeps price, quantity, and primary actions usable without critical clipping.
- Reduce Motion is honored for any custom badge/add animation; animation is optional and cannot block state changes.
- iOS and Android visual behavior remains consistent with existing app design tokens.
- No sensitive data is written to logs or storage because this prototype collects none.
notes: Do not add user accounts, remote sync, or order history as an error-recovery mechanism.

title: Add comprehensive unit, component, and integration tests for local cart flow
description:
Add deterministic automated coverage using the repository's existing test stack. Tests must use bundled Menu content or explicit local test fixtures through the same domain validation conventions; no mock HTTP server is needed because no cart path is allowed to use HTTP.

Coverage layers:
- Domain: reducer/store actions, quantity limits, selectors, cent arithmetic, reconciliation.
- Persistence: hydration ordering, schema validation, corrupt payload, stale item, clear.
- Menu components: add, current quantity, disabled/unpriced state.
- Cart screen: lines, editing, subtotal, empty state, clear, submit enabled/disabled.
- Navigation/badge: total-unit count and route behavior.
- Submit/confirmation: immutable receipt, double-submit guard, persisted clear, confirmation copy.

Where practical, assert that the cart/order modules have no dependency on configured API clients. Do not satisfy this by mocking fetch and continuing to call it; the implementation should simply have no network call.
acceptance_criteria:
- Cart domain tests cover all state transitions and money calculations.
- Persistence tests cover hydration race prevention, corruption, version mismatch, stale IDs, and clear-after-submit.
- Menu/Cart component tests cover key visual/interaction states and accessibility labels.
- Submit integration test proves receipt snapshot remains available after live cart is cleared.
- Integration test proves Menu quantity, badge count, and Cart line quantity stay in sync through one shared store.
- Test proves changed current Menu price is used after hydration rather than a stale persisted price.
- No cart test starts, mocks, or expects an HTTP/backend/order-provider service.
- Existing non-cart test suite remains passing or unrelated pre-existing failures are documented rather than hidden.
notes: Prefer deterministic fake local storage adapters in unit tests and one integration layer against the actual configured local persistence wrapper.

title: Add offline end-to-end cart acceptance flow for iOS and Android
description:
Add one critical E2E scenario (with platform-specific launcher configuration only where required) that validates the complete customer path using the release-like local/bundled architecture. The scenario must not start a backend, mock HTTP server, or external ordering provider.

Required path:
launch app -> Menu -> add at least two distinct priced items -> increment one quantity -> verify nonzero badge -> open Cart -> verify lines and subtotal -> decrement/remove one line as appropriate -> submit -> verify prototype confirmation wording and submitted summary -> return to Menu -> verify zero badge -> reopen Cart -> verify empty -> relaunch app -> verify cart remains empty.

Also add a persistence E2E variant or integration-level equivalent: add an item, relaunch before submit, and verify the local cart restores correctly. Execute on platforms available in the current environment; missing iOS runtime on Linux is not a code blocker, but cross-platform definitions/configuration must exist.
acceptance_criteria:
- Critical Menu -> Cart -> Submit -> Confirmation -> empty-cart path passes without any first-party API configuration.
- Network can be disabled for the cart E2E path without affecting success.
- Badge, quantities, line totals, and subtotal are verified at meaningful checkpoints.
- Successful submit leaves cart empty both immediately and after cold relaunch.
- Persistence-before-submit behavior is verified across relaunch at E2E or equivalent integration level.
- Confirmation visibly includes the no-real-order-transmitted prototype disclaimer.
- No test browses an external order URL or invokes an order-provider page.
- iOS/Android E2E definitions exist; execution is required on currently available platform runners.
notes: Do not make unavailable iOS hardware/simulator a reason to block Android/Linux code completion.

title: Document prototype boundaries and perform final local-cart acceptance
acceptance_criteria:
- oth-cart.1 through oth-cart.10 are closed.
- README/spec documentation accurately describes the local prototype cart and its limitations.
- Search of cart/order modules finds no fetch/axios/order-provider/web-scrape/payment integration.
- Release-like app with no OTH API configuration can add/edit/persist/submit/confirm/clear cart.
- Menu source-of-truth IDs/prices, storage key/schema, state architecture, and OrderSubmissionService seam are documented.
- Confirmation language cannot reasonably be mistaken for a real transmitted restaurant order.
- Existing Find Us/Event Detail functionality remains working and independent of this local Menu cart.
- Static typecheck/lint/unit/component/integration tests pass under repository conventions.
- E2E result is recorded for available platform(s), with unavailable platform runtime documented rather than treated as a backend blocker.
- No future-work item is represented as required for completion of this local prototype.
notes: This is the only intentionally blocked final acceptance bead in the cart epic.
